title: Want a Clean Heart?
excerpt: David made some terrible decisions, and still prayed "Create in me a clean heart." Why your past isn't too messed up for God to make you new.

blocks.text: King David made some great decisions, but he also made some terrible ones.

During his reign, David chose to abuse his power by sleeping with the wife of one of his military leaders, and then arranging for him to be pushed to the front lines of battle—where he was killed. For someone who was considered "a man after God's own heart," David really messed up.
In 2 Samuel 12:13, we see David confess his sin against the Lord and in Psalm 51, we see his prayer to be made new:

verses: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.

blocks.text: David failed, but God redeems. God restores. David still had to face the consequences of his decisions, but in that journey, God met him there.

If you want to be made new by God but believe that your past is too messed up, you can follow the path David showed us—confess, repent, and ask God to make you new. You can even use David's exact words as you pray: "Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me."
When we seek God, we realize that He's already been seeking us.
God is faithful. He loves you. He can make your heart clean. In Him, you can become a new creation.

God, forgive me when I sin and mess up. Create in me a clean heart and pure mind. I want to run into Your open arms instead of toward sin. Thank You for always being faithful to forgive me. You remain perfect when I am far from it. Help me to seek You daily. In Jesus's name, Amen.
